newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb explodes in Kashmir, seven wounded.
newsitem.headline: Bomb explodes in Kashmir, seven wounded.

text.p: A bomb exploded near the house of the chief minister of India's Jammu and Kashmir state, Farooq Abdullah, on Friday, Indian police said. Abdullah was not in the area at the time, they said.
Seven people were wounded by the blast, which went off some 30 metres (yards) from Abdullah's residence on Gupkar Road in the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir, Srinagar.

A police official said Abdullah, who escaped several attempts on his life during state assembly elections in September, was not in Srinagar when the land mine exploded on Friday. Abdullah's exact whereabouts were not known.
Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have died in Kashmir since a separatist revolt erupted in 1990.
On Wednesday, a junior minister in Abdullah's government escaped an attack by separatist guerrillas while he was paying his respects to his deceased father in a cemetery in Srinagar.
The militants threw two grenades which exploded about 50 metres (yards) from junior Home (Interior) Minister Mohmood Ahmad Sagar. One policeman was injured in Wednesday's attack.
